questions.enonce_markdown:
The scores of twenty students in a Physics test are recorded as follows:

$70\ \ 80\ \ 78\ \ 98\ \ 84\ \ 67\ \ 98\ \ 70\ \ 80\ \ 100$

$87\ \ 83\ \ 70\ \ 70\ \ 88\ \ 91\ \ 70\ \ 78\ \ 88\ \ 88$

Represent the above scores on a frequency distribution table.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Count how many times each score occurs (the tally of the $20$ values):

| Score $x$ | 67 | 70 | 78 | 80 | 83 | 84 | 87 | 88 | 91 | 98 | 100 | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency $f$ | 1 | 5 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 3 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 20 |
| $f \times x$ | 67 | 350 | 156 | 160 | 83 | 84 | 87 | 264 | 91 | 196 | 100 | 1638 |

The frequencies add up to $20$, the number of students, so no score has been missed.

questions.enonce_markdown: Determine the mode of the distribution.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The mode is the score with the highest frequency. The score $70$ occurs $5$ times (next is $88$ with $3$).

**Answer: mode $= 70$.**

There are $20$ scores (an even number), so the median is the mean of the $10$th and $11$th scores when they are in order.

Ordered: $67,\ 70,\ 70,\ 70,\ 70,\ 70,\ 78,\ 78,\ 80,\ 80,\ 83,\ 84,\ 87,\ 88,\ 88,\ 88,\ 91,\ 98,\ 98,\ 100$.

The $10$th score is $80$ and the $11$th is $83$: median $= \dfrac{80 + 83}{2} = 81.5$.

**Answer: median $= 81.5$.**
